## Why is $fx$ useful for the mean? {#l2-why-fx}

The frequency tells us **how many times a value occurs**. The product $fx$ just means $f\times x$.

Four households have three pets each:

$$3+3+3+3=4\times3=12.$$

Adding all the $fx$ values gives the **sum of all the individual data values**—the numerator when calculating the mean.

$$\bar{x}=\frac{\text{sum of }fx\text{ values}}{\text{sum of }f\text{ values}}.$$

::: {.notation-key}
$\sum fx$ means **sum of the $fx$ values**; $\sum f$ means **sum of the $f$ values**.
:::

::: notes
Connect multiplication to repeated addition before adding the new column. Here fx counts the pets contributed by each group of households; adding the products gives 56 pets. Adding the frequencies gives 50 households. Sigma is new notation: say 'sum of' each time it appears. Do not average the distinct x-values without using their frequencies.
:::
